h: Stag, Hen or Just a Gang of Mates
p: Brighton pulls in big groups every weekend, and karting has become a classic way to kick off a celebration. If you're organising, a little planning keeps the day running smoothly. Get numbers confirmed early, book a slot well ahead for summer Saturdays, and make sure everyone knows the meeting time, not just the race time.
Keep the fancy dress for later. Loose costumes, capes and inflatable accessories don't belong in a kart, and you'll be asked to leave them off anyway. Save the outfits for the evening.

Likewise, save the drinking until after the racing. You'll need a clear head and quick reactions, and staff won't let anyone race who's had a few. It's much more fun to celebrate the podium with a pint than miss out on the race altogether.

And if you're coming in for the weekend, Brighton station has direct trains from London, Gatwick and along the coast, so nobody needs to drive and everyone can enjoy the evening that follows the race.

Once the helmets are off, the Palace Pier is a classic for a wander, and the seafront between there and Hove is great for a sunset stroll. The Brighton Toy and Model Museum, tucked under the station, is a quirky stop for anyone who loves tiny cars as well as fast ones.
